sentences.text: Gondwanatitan was a titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur.
This animal was relatively small for its group, measuring about 7 meters in length and weighing roughly 1 tonne.
Its limb bones were relatively gracile.

The species is distinguished by unique features including heart-shaped distal articular surfaces of proximal and middle caudal vertebrae, a developed and medially curved deltopectoral crest on the humerus, and a tibia with a dorsally projecting anterior proximal joint and a laterally curved cnemial crest.
The middle tail vertebrae are distinctively heart-shaped, a feature that helps distinguish them from those of Aeolosaurus.
The middle tail vertebrae also had elongated centra.
The type specimen of Gondwanatitan faustoi was discovered in 1983 on the farm of Yoshitoshi Myzobuchi in São Paulo, Brazil.
The type specimen was excavated between 1984 and 1986, with serious preparation work beginning in 1997.
Some elements of the holotype were lost in the National Museum of Brazil fire on September 2, 2018, though several elements survived and were recovered.
Gondwanatitan is a member of the clade Aeolosauridae.

Although its phylogenetic position is unclear, Gondwanatitan is not closely linked to members of Saltasaurinae and can be distinguished from more basal titanosaurians like Andesaurus and Malawisaurus.
Aeolosaurus is considered the closest relative of Gondwanatitan.
Gondwanatitan lived in Brazil during the late Cretaceous Period, approximately 70 million years ago, when the region was part of the supercontinent Gondwana.
Gondwanatitan lived in South America during the late Cretaceous Period, approximately 83 million years ago in the Santonian stage.
It is debated whether Gondwanatitan is a valid genus; it was briefly considered a junior synonym of Aeolosaurus in 2001 but is now widely regarded as separate.
